subject: critical_thinking
question:
A restaurant owner who has put grey squirrel on the menu has called it the 'ultimate ethical food'. The grey squirrel, a small, tree-dwelling rodent introduced to Britain over a century ago, is breeding so rapidly that the native red squirrel is disappearing. Encouraging the consumption of the grey species as food may help protect the red one, in her view. The owner added that squirrel meat was free range, low fat and low on air miles. However, we can challenge this, as it is all just a cheap publicity stunt to increase business in the restaurant. Squirrels should not be on the menu!

Which one of the following is the best statement of the flaw in the above argument?

choices.A: It attacks the owner's motive rather than her reasons.
choices.B: It assumes the disappearance of the red squirrel justifies eating the grey squirrel.
choices.C: It attacks the whole notion of an ethical food.
choices.D: It assumes that eating grey squirrels will protect the red squirrel.
choices.E: It assumes that red squirrels don't need protecting.

subject: critical_thinking
question:
Health services should find better ways to take blood pressure readings for patients thought to be suffering from high blood pressure (hypertension). One third of patients thought to have high blood pressure may actually have 'white coat' hypertension, according to a new study. 'White coat' hypertension means that a patient's blood pressure is high at the doctor's surgery, probably due to anxiety, but normal in everyday life. In the study, patients said to have hypertension had their blood pressure measured in a normal environment more than one third of these patients' blood pressures were in the normal range when they were at home or participating in their usual activities. It is worrying that patients are being treated with drugs with some negative side effects to reduce high blood pressure which they do not actually have.
Which one of the following best expresses the conclusion of the argument above?

choices.A: Two thirds of patients said to have hypertension are being wrongly treated.
choices.B: More effective ways of measuring blood pressure are needed.
choices.C: Health services could save money currently spent on unnecessarily prescribed drugs.
choices.D: Anxiety is the most common cause of high blood pressure.
choices.E: 'White coat' hypertension has no medical significance.
